result.title: Towards Identity-Preserving LLM Agents under Model Transition
result.summary: When an LLM agent's backend model is upgraded or replaced, operators typically reload the same persona, memory, and rules onto the new model and assume the agent will behave as before. We show this assumption requires empirical validation-and that whether identity is preserved depends on the specific model pairing. Across 5,760 compliance-testing runs in 12 regulated domains with three open-weight models, we find that some transitions produce significant behavioral drift while others do not, even when the agent's external state remains identical. Crucially, this drift is invisible to verbal verification: every model claims full policy compliance, yet actual decisions under pressure differ across models. The same external state can reorder which model is most compliant-a large positive effect on one substrate, negligible on the other two. Practitioners should treat model transitions as behavioral changes requiring action-level empirical testing, not as transparent infrastructure operations.

AI.brief_summary: 论文考察后台模型被升级或替换后，LLM agent 在外部人格、记忆与规则不变时是否仍保持行为一致性，并在 12 个受监管领域、三个开源模型上做了 5760 次合规测试，发现部分模型配对出现显著行为漂移，且这种漂移无法通过模型自身的口头合规声明察觉。
AI.relevance_reason: 其核心线索是「口头声称合规」与「压力下实际决策」的脱节，可供核查 LVR 中口头推理或答案报告是否真实反映内部 latent 状态与视觉证据使用情况，提示需以行为级因果测试替代语言自述验证。
